extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's Foundations)
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of definitions, preservation criteria, and techniques about how common properties of morphisms and schemes behave under base change, geometric fibers, and normalization; includes constructions such as the Segre embedding. Intended as textbook guidance for reasoning about schemes and morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally finitely presented morphisms and reduction to Noetherian case
rubrics_metrics.description: Each finitely presented morphism is locally (on the base) a pullback of a finite type morphism to a Noetherian scheme; hence any result proved for Noetherian schemes and stable under base change is automatically proved for locally finitely presented morphisms to arbitrary schemes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When proving statements for locally finitely presented morphisms, reduce locally on the base to the finite-type-to-Noetherian case and then use base-change stability. Use the full definition of finite presentation when needed (exercise hint: treat affine case first, glue via affine opens).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chevalley’s Constructibility Theorem (locally finitely presented case)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) If A is a finitely presented B-algebra A = B[x1,..,xn]/(f1,..,fr), then the image of Spec A -> Spec B is a finite union of locally closed subsets. (b) If π:X→Y is quasicompact and locally finitely presented and Y is quasicompact, then π(X) is a finite union of locally closed subsets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part (a) reduces to an affine exercise; part (b) follows by covering Y and X and using (a). The general form of Chevalley (in EGA) treats local constructibility and finitely presented maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of open embeddings under base change
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of 'open embedding' is preserved by base change (Exercise 8.1.D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check by describing the fibered product: the preimage of an open embedding is the open subscheme ψ^{-1}(Y) and satisfies the universal property of the fibered product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of closed embeddings under base change
rubrics_metrics.description: Closed embeddings are preserved by base change (see §10.2(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given a Cartesian diagram with Y→Z a closed embedding, the pulled-back W→X is a closed embedding. Check on affine patches / ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of locally closed embeddings under base change
rubrics_metrics.description: Locally closed embeddings are preserved under base change; intersections of locally closed subschemes can be defined scheme-theoretically via pullback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that open and closed embeddings are preserved and glue to get locally closed behavior; verify compatibility with previous definitions of intersections of opens/closed subschemes (Exercises 10.4.A, 10.4.B).

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally principal closed subschemes pull back to locally principal
rubrics_metrics.description: Locally principal closed subschemes (Definition 9.5.1) pull back to locally principal closed subschemes under base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check locally where defining equations become principal; see Exercise 10.4.C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasicompactness preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: The property 'quasicompact' of a morphism is preserved under base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is listed among the standard 'reasonable' properties (Exercise 10.4.D(a)); verify locality on the target and stability under base change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine morphism preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: Being an affine morphism is preserved under base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check on affine targets and use the tensor product description of pulled-back algebras (Exercise 10.4.D(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite morphism preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: The property 'finite' for morphisms is preserved by base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the affine characterization (finite as finite module) and tensor with the target ring to check preservation (Exercise 10.4.D(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral morphism preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: Integral morphisms are preserved under base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to affine case and use integrality of rings and base change along ring maps (Exercise 10.4.D(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally of finite type preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: The property 'locally of finite type' of morphisms is preserved under base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work locally on source and target, present rings as finitely generated algebras, and check behavior under tensor product (Exercise 10.4.D(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite type preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: Being of finite type is preserved by base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same reductions as locally finite type but with quasicompactness; see Exercise 10.4.D(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Locally of finite presentation preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: The property 'locally of finite presentation' is preserved by base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is starred in Exercise 10.4.D(g); use finite presentation of algebras and the fact finite presentation is stable under base change and localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quasi-finite morphism preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: The notion of 'quasi-finite morphism' (finite type + finite fibres) is preserved by base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: 'finite fibres' alone is not preserved by base change; reduce to the affine case Spec A -> Spec k and use finiteness criteria and previous preservation results (Exercise 10.4.F).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surjectivity preserved by base change
rubrics_metrics.description: Surjectivity of morphisms (as maps of underlying sets) is preserved by base change; surjective morphisms form a 'reasonable' class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof may use field tensor products and existence of maximal ideals (Axiom of Choice). See Exercise 10.4.G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity is not preserved by base change; use universally injective (radicial) instead
rubrics_metrics.description: Injectivity can fail after base change (e.g., Spec C -> Spec R). Define 'universally injective' (radicial) morphisms as those that remain injective after any base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monomorphisms are universally injective. To test universal injectivity, check that each fiber has at most one point after any base change; equivalently (Exercise 10.5.I) π is universally injective iff π is injective and for each point p the field extension κ(p)/κ(π(p)) is purely inseparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universally P morphism (general patch)
rubrics_metrics.description: If P is some property of schemes, a morphism is 'universally P' if it remains P after any base change; the class of universally P morphisms is preserved by base change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Universally P is often the correct fix when a property P is not preserved by base change; producing equivalent criteria (so you don't have to check all base changes) is essential in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric point and geometric fiber definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A geometric point of X is a map Spec k -> X with k algebraically closed. A geometric fiber of X->Y is the fiber over a geometric point Spec k -> Y, i.e., the fibered product with that geometric point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric points encode a point plus an embedding of its residue field into an algebraically closed field; geometric fibers are used to define 'geometrically X' properties of fibers and schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometrically connected/irreducible/integral/reduced fibers and schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism has geometrically connected/irreducible/integral/reduced fibers if all its geometric fibers have that property. A k-scheme X is geometrically connected/irreducible/integral/reduced if X×_k Spec K has the property for all field extensions K/k (various equivalent formulations are given: CK, CK=K, Ck, Cks, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although definition requires checking all algebraically closed field extensions, often failure/success is detected after a finite extension; many equivalences (Harder fact 10.5.3) reduce checks to separable or perfect closures in practice. See Exercises 10.5.B–10.5.F and subsequent propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing geometric properties via finite/separable/perfect closures
rubrics_metrics.description: There are twelve related statements (CK, CK=K, Ck, Cks, etc.) for connected/irreducible/reduced; many implications are trivial, and the harder fact is that these sets of statements are equivalent (under suitable hypotheses), so geometric properties can be checked after finite/separable/perfect extensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exercises 10.5.F, 10.5.3 (Harder fact), and later propositions (10.5.12, 10.5.15, etc.) to reduce checks to manageable field extensions (e.g., to k, its separable or perfect closure, or finite extensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor-finiteness trick
rubrics_metrics.description: Any single element of a tensor product is a finite sum of elementary tensors, so one can pass to the subring generated by the tensor components (a finitely-generated algebra) to reduce many arguments to the finite type case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly to reduce statements about arbitrary schemes/algebras to statements about finitely-generated algebras over fields, enabling the use of classical geometry over algebraically closed fields (see §10.5.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectedness/irreducibility over separably closed base fields
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is separably closed and Spec A is connected (resp. irreducible), then Spec A⊗_k K is connected (resp. irreducible) for any field extension K/k; hence connectedness and irreducibility are preserved when the base is separably closed (Propositions 10.5.10, 10.5.14, Corollary 10.5.12, Proposition 10.5.15).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs use the tensor-finiteness trick and the fact that Spec of a structure map is universally open (Fact 10.5.6). This gives a practical method: if base field is separably closed, connected/irreducible properties automatically become geometrically so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reducedness and perfect fields (geometric reducedness criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is geometrically reduced and A is reduced, then A⊗_k B is reduced (Prop. 10.5.18). For perfect base fields k, reducedness is well-behaved under extension: for E/k an extension of a perfect field and X reduced over k, X_E is reduced (Prop.10.5.21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Algebraic Fact 10.5.17 (finitely generated extensions of perfect fields are separably generated) and the tensor-finiteness trick; reduce to the affine/finitely generated case and then to fields to check reducedness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normalization of reduced/integral schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: A normalization of a reduced scheme X is a morphism ν: X~ -> X from a normal scheme which induces a bijection of irreducible components and satisfies a universal property (hence unique up to unique isomorphism). For X = Spec A integral, the normalization is Spec of the integral closure of A in its fraction field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normalization exists for affine integral schemes via integral closure; normalizations are integral and surjective (Exercise 10.7.C). Normalizations of integral schemes exist in general (Exercise 10.7.B). Extend definition to reduced schemes with finitely-many irreducible components (locally Noetherian case) by applying normalization on components (Exercise 10.7.D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Segre embedding: product of projective schemes as closed embedding
rubrics_metrics.description: The Segre morphism P^m_A ×_A P^n_A -> P^{mn+m+n}_A given by ([x],[y]) ↦ [x_i y_j] is a well-defined morphism and is a closed embedding; its image (Segre variety) is cut out scheme-theoretically by vanishing of all 2×2 minors (rank-one condition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check locally on affine charts (Exercise 10.6.A); for coordinate-free description see Exercise 10.6.C. The m=n=1 case yields the quadric surface with equation a00 a11 - a01 a10 = 0. The gluing and surjectivity checks use explicit affine maps zab/ij ↦ x_a/i y_b/j.
